headline: Histology, spots and unpaired omics are translated into cell-resolved molecular profiles
label: Cross Modal Spatial Omics Inference
summary: GeneFlow, SCOPE, st2sc and SpOTr infer cell-resolved expression or protein from coarser or cheaper inputs such as H&E images or spot-level spatial data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is predicting one molecular layer from another, often at finer resolution. GeneFlow uses flow matching with histology and gene tokenizers to predict panels of up to 1,000 spatial genes from histology. SCOPE predicts single-cell RNA and protein from H&E using RNA-protein biomarker priors across 16 organs. st2sc infers single-cell expression from multicellular spots with an attention-based transformer, and SpOTr couples Fused Gromov-Wasserstein transport with spot deconvolution to map single cells onto spatial data. A rotation-equivariant network reconstructs 3D cell shape from transcript point clouds, and these embeddings improve protein prediction. A second strand addresses unpaired or multimodal integration: SCALEMAP self-maps for diagonal integration, GatorAnchor refines cross-modal neighborhoods with uncertainty-aware representations, and multiCAsp adds a graph-Laplacian spatial prior to canonical association. The shift from earlier transformer-centric single-cell work is toward generative and transport-based inference anchored in spatial and histological context.
